newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks soar to record close.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks soar to record close.

text.p: A confident Australian share market smashed records to close higher on Thursday with traders in an upbeat mood as big banks and miners showed the way up.

The All Ordinaries index jumped 22.9 points to 2,496.4 after hitting a record and intraday high of 2,500.9, surpassing the previous record high of 2,479.1, reached on February 12. The previous record close was 2,473.5, also on February 12.
Traders said the cocktail of stronger metals prices, growth prospects of the yield-rich big banks and a soaring Wall Street proved to be a heady mix for enthusiastic investors.
"It's been a very exciting day and we've seen some big money come into the market," said Greg Matthews, executive director of Australian equities at Mercantile Mutual Investment Management.
"Banks had a great day, the golds and metals companies are up, clearly on the back of stronger metal prices overseas, and the Dow is up. Everything has come together today."
National Australia Bank led the booming bank sector higher, jumping 2.8 percent to close at A$16.52 (US$12.66).
The big banks climbed to record highs in early trading before all except National Australia Bank succumbed to profit taking near their fresh peaks.
The major miners were firmer across the board, the gold sector impressing with a 1.9 percent jump.

Shares in property developer/financial services group Lend Lease Corp jumped after the company announced a 14.2 percent rise in first half net profit of A$160 million but ended 11 cents lower at A$23.00. Brokers said the strong price rise had proved too tempting for sellers.
It was also big day for media stocks results.
Prime Television shares closed five cents higher at A$2.55 after the company reported a 21.6 percent rise in first half net profit to A$7.98 million.
Rural Press reported a four percent higher first half net profit of A$16.96 million after trading closed. Its shares ended at A$4.10, steady on the day.
PMP Communications was unchanged after its 2.6 percent lower first half net profit of A$30.55 million.
In the resources, results came from contract miner Eltin whose shares ended eight cents higher at A$2.73 after the company said it more than doubled first half net profit.
Placer Dome's 77 percent owned Placer Pacific reported a full year net profit of A$43.2 million and its shares closed four cents higher at A$1.78.

Media giant News Corp shared in the market's good cheer early but retreated to end slight lower at A$6.71. Traders said the focus of the day was elsewhere with a soft result from its 40.4 percent owned PMP Communications also failing to help.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about two to one, while about 25 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
